name: Jackson Square
desc: Artists, fortune tellers, and a cathedral photobombing every shot. Costs nothing, feels like the center of the universe at midnight.

name: St. Louis Cathedral
desc: That triple-spired postcard you have already screenshotted. Step inside for free and let the AC and the hush do their thing.

name: National WWII Museum
desc: A whole campus of history that eats an entire day. Pricey, yes, but this is the splurge you plan around for months.

name: City Park
desc: Ancient oaks dripping with moss, bigger than Central Park, and free. Bring the dog and a daydream, leave with both happier.

name: Frenchmen Street
desc: Live jazz spills out of every doorway after dark. Wandering the sidewalk with zero dollars is a legitimate concert ticket here.

name: Preservation Hall
desc: A tiny wooden room where jazz gets played the old way, no phones, no drinks, all goosebumps. Worth skipping lunches for.

name: St. Charles Streetcar
desc: A dollar and a quarter buys you a rattling mansion tour under the oaks. Cheapest time machine in America.

name: French Market
desc: Open-air stalls of hot sauce, trinkets, and snacks by the river. Browse hungry, leave with exactly one weird treasure.

name: Crescent Park
desc: A rusty-chic riverside walk where the Mississippi bends and the skyline glows. Free front-row seats to barge-watching.

name: Garden District Stroll
desc: Self-guided mansion envy under live oaks. Pick your future house, argue about paint colors, spend nothing.
